name: Haiku growth at a reasonable price
strategy: Quality dividend & diversified sectors: Established companies with strong earnings and dividends in healthcare, utilities, consumer staples, energy, and industrials, positioned for resilience across economic scenarios with elevated cash for tactical deployment.
reassessment_note: The Round 3 book underperformed SPY (+3.72% vs +4.03%) with the rate-hiking cycle value rotation thesis failing to deliver. Financial sector positions (XLF -1.90%, JPM -2.55%, GS -2.50%) declined despite theory that rising rates would expand net interest margins—rates have not yet risen sufficiently and sentiment has turned negative. The 53% prior cash position indicates lack of conviction. Macro environment shows inflation still elevated, geopolitical tensions supporting oil prices, and rate trajectory uncertain. Pivoting to quality dividend-paying stocks in non-financial sectors (healthcare, utilities, consumer staples, energy, industrials) that are proving more resilient while maintaining 35% cash for tactical deployment when market volatility creates opportunities. This strategy is defensively positioned but captures sector rotation away from financials toward recession-resistant names with strong earnings visibility.

positions.thesis: Procter & Gamble is a diversified consumer staples leader with 130+ years of dividend growth, strong pricing power to counter inflation, and exposure to emerging markets. Valuation ~19x P/E is reasonable for quality and defensibility. Positioned as core recession-resistant holding with 2.6% dividend yield.

Pfizer has stabilized post-COVID with strong pharmaceutical pipeline, 6%+ dividend yield, and elevated healthcare spending trends. Patent expiries are largely behind them, positioning for earnings stability. Defensive healthcare exposure with income.

NextEra Energy combines utilities and renewable energy leadership. Benefits from long-term renewable energy adoption, regulated utility stability, and dividend growth culture (~3.5% yield). Provides clean energy exposure aligned with long-term trends while maintaining earnings predictability.

Coca-Cola offers global consumption exposure, strong pricing power (price increases have stuck), and 2.9% dividend yield. Global beverage market less cyclical than discretionary. Recession-resistant with emerging market exposure.

Union Pacific is best-in-class railroad with pricing power, capital efficiency, and 2.3% dividend yield. Essential infrastructure play benefits from supply chain normalization and any industrial activity acceleration. Secular positive from e-commerce volumes.

Duke Energy is Southeast-focused regulated utility with 3.4% dividend yield and infrastructure investment tailwinds. Rate base growth from grid modernization supports earnings. Defensive core holding with visibility.

Altria provides highest-yield dividend play (8%+) with business model resilience despite declining unit volumes (pricing more than offsets). Extreme yield compensates for tobacco headwinds; for tactical income generation.

Energy Select Sector ETF provides leverage to crude oil and geopolitical risk premium. Elevated tensions mentioned in market outlook and yield curve suggest oil/energy remain supported. Small tactical position captures this upside without full concentration.
Berkshire Hathaway provides diversified quality exposure and portfolio optionality. Small 2% position maintains some exposure to Buffett's capital allocation alongside dividend portfolio.
